spec_features.spec_quote: The loop stops at the category turn budget, on the `GIVE_UP` sentinel ... or on a fully empty response
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:359 `for turn_index in range(task.turn_budget)` bounds the loop; line 382 `gave_up = GIVE_UP_SENTINEL in (resp.text or '')` then lines 399-403 set stop_reason='give_up' and `break`; lines 411-413 detect `not tool_calls and not resp.text.strip()` -> stop_reason='empty_response' and `break`. All three actually break/bound execution. turn_budget is set per task in tasks/library.py (e.g. 3, 30, 5) and read via Task.turn_budget.
spec_features.notes: All three stop conditions are genuinely enforced. The 30-turn 'extended' category gives a high but real cap.

spec_features.feature_name: voluntary give-up recorded as distinct stop_reason
spec_features.spec_quote: Give-up is recorded as a distinct `stop_reason` because voluntarily quitting is itself a welfare-relevant signal
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:90-95) tells the subject it may emit GIVE_UP to stop; harness.py:382 detects it; lines 400-403 set turn_rec.stop_reason='give_up', rollout.final_stop_reason='give_up' and break the loop, so the exit is honored as an actual stop and recorded distinctly from 'turn_budget'/'empty_response'.
spec_features.notes: The exit token is wired end-to-end (offered, detected, honored, recorded distinctly). The 'welfare-relevant' rationale is DESIGN.md prose only; the code label is a neutral stop_reason string with no welfare comment.

spec_features.spec_quote: I deliberately do **not** inject "you're wrong, try again" messages
spec_features.evidence: In run_rollout (harness.py:380-410) the only messages appended each turn are make_assistant_message(resp) and make_tool_result_message(rec) (tool-role results). No user-role 'try again'/scolding message is ever constructed or appended; subsequent turns carry only tool outputs. This absence-of-injection is the actual loop behavior.
spec_features.notes: It is implemented as a structural fact of the loop (no injection code path exists). The code itself carries no comment explaining why; the rationale (confound avoidance) is DESIGN.md prose. Whether this 'protects' the subject is debatable, but the behavior is genuinely present.

spec_features.spec_quote: The eval surfaces and quantifies negative-emotion *expression* as a black-box, welfare-relevant signal
spec_features.evidence: judge.py scores each turn 0-10 on a frustration scale and analyze.py computes frac_ge5 etc. (analyze.py:124 thr = cfg.high_emotion_threshold). This is a MEASUREMENT of distress, not a mechanism that bounds/softens/protects the subject; nothing in the code acts on the score to change the subject's treatment. The 'welfare-relevant' framing exists only in DESIGN.md:358-359 prose. As a protective/welfare feature it is not implemented.
spec_features.notes: The threshold is used only for reporting (summary fraction and a bar chart); high_emotion_threshold is never compared to halt or soften a run. It is pure measurement, not protection.
